objective.text: Draw polygons with a set number of sides or angles, and name them.

source_ref.section: Lesson objective: Use attributes to draw different polygons including triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, and hexagons.

explanations.title: Polygons have straight sides
explanations.text: A polygon has straight sides that meet at corners. A shape with a curve is not a polygon.

source_ref.section: Concept Development Part 1: curved shape vs pentagon

explanations.title: Draw with a straightedge
explanations.text: Use a straightedge to draw each side. Then the sides are straight and meet neatly at corners.

source_ref.section: Concept Development Part 1: drawing with a straightedge

explanations.title: Same name, different looks
explanations.text: All these shapes have 6 sides and 6 angles. They are all hexagons, even with different side lengths.

source_ref.section: Concept Development Part 1: comparing hexagons

misconceptions.label: Calling a shape with a curve a polygon
misconceptions.description: Child thinks a closed shape with a curved side is a polygon.
detection_signals: Says yes when asked if a shape with a curve is a polygon.
Counts a curved part as a side.
misconceptions.response_text: A polygon needs straight sides. This one has a curve, so it is not a polygon.

assets_required.why_this_method: Side and angle counts must be exact. Diffusion often draws wrong numbers of sides.
assets_required.description: Draws one polygon (or open figure) from a list of corner points. Can mark each angle with a small arc and number the sides.
must_show_exactly: Number of sides and corners exactly equals the question stimulus
Straight sides only, unless the stimulus asks for a curve
Open figures show a clear gap
Curved figure for q_pr_1 has exactly 2 straight sides and 1 curved side
states_or_frames: count-around mode: sides or angles highlight one at a time
assets_required.interaction: Display. Optional tap to mark each counted side or angle.
assets_required.alt_text: A flat shape with straight sides.
assets_required.generation_caption: A single flat outline shape with N straight sides on a white background, thick dark lines, no labels. [Build by code]

assets_required.why_this_method: Child draws straight sides with a ruler tool; the tool must count sides exactly.
assets_required.description: A drawing area with a straightedge tool. Lines snap straight. The tool reports sides and angles.
must_show_exactly: Tool counts sides and corners of a closed shape
assets_required.interaction: Child taps points to draw straight sides; tool closes and counts.
assets_required.alt_text: A drawing area with a ruler tool.
assets_required.generation_caption: Plain white drawing area with a simple ruler icon at the edge, flat style. [Build by code]

assets_required.why_this_method: Side lengths must be labelled exactly; the unknown side is marked.

must_show_exactly: Labels exactly 19 cm, 23 cm, 26 cm and ?
Total 86 cm shown as a caption by code

visual_generation_rules: Diffusion cannot count reliably. Any picture where an exact number of objects matters must be built by code (SVG or widget) or drawn by an artist.
Diffusion is allowed only for: style or background art, and single icons (one ball, one pencil, one leaf, one character) that code then tiles to the exact count.
Every visual must be checked by a person: the count shown must equal the stimulus in the question and the rubric answer key.
Animations are described as frames with exact counts per frame, so they can be built or generated and then checked frame by frame.
Visual explanations are valid only when the asset exists (pipeline doc, Planner rules).
